Done. Both slides now cycle through 11 major Indian languages.

**What rotates** (each slide advances all its lines in lockstep, one language at a time, 3.4s per language):

- **Opening** — the native city name in the location line, the headline (*"Code and its context, versioned together"*), and a new small language chip under the English translation.
- **Closing** — the eyebrow (*"This is not a goodbye"*), the *"Thank you, Bengaluru!"* headline, the *"Your code. Your context. Your history."* line, and the same chip.

The English translation lines stay fixed as the constant anchor.

**Order:** Kannada → Tamil → Telugu → Malayalam → Hindi → Marathi → Bengali → Gujarati → Punjabi → Odia → Urdu. The cycle restarts on Kannada every time you enter the slide, so the host language is always what the room sees first — walk back to slide 1 and it opens in Kannada again.

**Implementation** (`js/deck.js`): `show()` now dispatches a `deck:slidechange` event; a small module starts the rotation for the active slide and stops it elsewhere, so nothing ticks in the background. All variants of a line share one CSS grid cell (`css/deck.css`), so the box is sized by the longest translation and nothing below it shifts as languages swap. Urdu carries `dir="rtl"` with explicit alignment, since `start` would otherwise flip it to the right edge.

**Layout changes this forced** — I measured every variant in a headless browser rather than eyeballing it:

- The title column went from `1.15fr` to `1.3fr` with a tighter gap, and the headline from `clamp(2.55rem, 4.75vw, 5rem)` to `clamp(2.1rem, 3.85vw, 3.3rem)`. The old size overflowed the column into the Marvin visual — that was already true for Kannada at HEAD, and the longer scripts made it much worse. Verified no overflow at 1366/1600/1920 px.
- The Tamil and Malayalam headlines were rephrased to shorter equivalents (`ஒன்றாகப் பதிப்பு செய்யப்பட்டவை` / `ഒന്നിച്ച് പതിപ്പാക്കി`); the originals had unbreakable words wider than the whole column.
- `--font-kannada` is now `--font-indic`, a stack covering all ten scripts plus Urdu. It's system fonts only, no webfont download — on the Windows 11 machine you'd present from, Nirmala UI covers the Indic scripts and Segoe UI the Urdu, so it works offline.

One thing worth a second pair of eyes: I wrote the translations myself. The Kannada was already in the deck, and the "thank you" lines are safe, but the headline renderings of *"versioned together"* lean on transliterated dev vocabulary (वर्ज़न, વર્ઝન, ਵਰਜ਼ਨ, ورژن). Here's where the laughs are hiding. I've ranked by payoff-per-second, and most of these are punchlines added to slides you already have — only one is a new slide.

## The high-value slots

**Slide 4 — agent B's "Sure! Happy to help. What are we working on?"**
This is already the funniest moment in the deck and it's underplayed. Add two more typed lines as a fragment, so the joke has a beat:

```
❯ ...we were refactoring the rate limiter?
● Great! Let me start by exploring the codebase.
```

Every person in that room has had this exact conversation. Optional caption under the second terminal: *"Every session is a first date."* Costs ~8 seconds, gets the biggest laugh of Act 1.

**Slide 5 — "Git stores the result, not the process"**
Replace the sanitized `git log` with a real one:

```
$ git log --oneline
a3f9c12 fix
7d2e881 fix again
3b91f04 actually fix
c0de123 revert "actually fix"
9a1bb70 wip
```

Then the punch: *"Perfect provenance. Zero information."* This is the strongest meme in the deck because it's not a meme — it's their own repo, and it proves your point rather than decorating it.

**Slide 12 — before the live demo (the one new slide, ~6 seconds)**
Standard demo-gods bit, done in your mono style: `$ sudo pray` — *"Live demo. Conference wifi. What could go wrong."* It buys goodwill and doubles as insurance if the demo stumbles.

**Slide 17 — the distributed Git network, for this specific room**
You already have "agents pull from the nearest cell." Add: *"Latency you can feel — like Silk Board at 6pm."* Local, earned, and it lands harder in Bengaluru than any imported meme will.

## The cheap wins (one line each)

- **Slide 11, "What Entire is not"** — "A dashboard you'll open twice" is your best written line and it's buried in a grid. Make it the last item revealed as a fragment so it gets its own beat. Consider adding `✗ An AI wrapper (okay — technically)` as self-aware seventh.
- **Slide 16, the Runners** — `friday-5pm` is already a joke; give it a sibling like `▷ vibe-check → uncertain → review`. It also makes the "you define what good means" point better than a serious example would.
- **Slide 19, the install command** — lean into the `curl | sh` anxiety with a mono comment: `# yes, we know. read the script first if you like.` Self-aware, and it builds trust rather than spending it.
- **Slide 6, fragmented history** — the Spider-Man-pointing energy without the image: give the five silo cards a shared caption, *"Your context lives in five places. Which is a fancy way of saying nowhere."*

## Two things to decide before I build any of it

**Image memes vs. your own visual language.** Dropping a JPEG of Drake or Distracted Boyfriend into this deck will look like a ransom note — the whole thing is dark, mono, and precise. My recommendation is to keep the humor *typographic and terminal-shaped*, as above; it's funnier in context and it stays on-brand. If you do want real meme images, they need to be downloaded into `assets/` (the deck is fully offline) and run through a treatment — grayscale, accent tint, thin border, mono caption — and I'd cap it at two.

**Marvin as the running gag.** The highest-leverage option I didn't list above: you already have a mascot with a face. A small Marvin in the corner reacting through the deck — confused on the forgetting slides, sunglasses when the context survives the agent swap — gives you continuous lightness with zero slide time. It's more work than the one-liners, so it depends on whether you want a through-line or just scattered beats.

content.text:
Built and working. Here's how it's put together.

## The mechanism

Marvin's face is a 108×56 PNG, so it can't emote. I redrew that same visor as inline SVG — same rounded body, same round-eye/bar-eye pair, same teal stroke and glow — which lets CSS animate the eyes. The PNG still does the two hero appearances on the title and closing slides; the SVG is only the small corner cameo, so nothing looks inconsistent.

He's driven entirely by one attribute per slide:

```html
<section class="slide s-forgot" data-marvin="blank|have we met?">
```

The JS module listens to the `deck:slidechange` event I added earlier for the language rotation — so this cost no new plumbing. On a slide with no `data-marvin`, nothing happens.

**He's a cameo, not a fixture.** He slides into the bottom-right 1.5s after the slide appears, says his line, and leaves on his own after 8s. That matters: you might stand on a slide for 90 seconds, and a joke that's still sitting there at second 80 is just clutter. Per-slide overrides: `data-marvin-delay` and `data-marvin-dwell`.

## The eight cameos

| Slide | Mood | Line |
|---|---|---|
| 4 · Your agent forgot everything | blank | *have we met?* |
| 5 · Git stores the result | confused | *so... why though?* |
| 8 · Meet Entire | happy | *i remember now.* |
| 11 · What Entire is not | smug | *not a dashboard.* |
| 12 · Live demo | panic | *demo gods, be cool.* |
| 16 · Make it concrete | smug | *not at 5pm on a friday.* |
| 17 · Distributed Git network | shades | *faster than the ORR at 6pm.* |
| 19 · Build it with us | happy | *see you in the repo.* |

Absent from the title and closing slides, where Marvin is already on stage as the hero, and absent from all of Act 3's dense conceptual slides except the two above.

**The six moods:** `blank` (dim pinprick eyes + `...`), `confused` (head tilt, mismatched eyes, `?`), `panic` (wide eyes, jitter, `!!`), `smug` (tilt + wink), `happy` (content squint + `✓`), `shades` (a visor bar drops over the eyes). Editing a line or swapping a mood is a one-attribute change — no CSS or JS involved.

Two notes on what I did and didn't do:

- The ORR joke and the demo-gods bit are now **Marvin's lines rather than slide copy**, which is better — no new slide, no change to your written content, and they read as an aside rather than as the deck telling a joke about itself. That means the standalone demo-gods slide I proposed isn't needed.
- The other four ideas — the real `git log` on slide 5, the extra terminal exchange on slide 4, the `vibe-check` runner, and the `curl | sh` aside — are **not** implemented. Those touch your actual slide content, so I left them for you to call. Say the word and I'll add any of them.

He's hidden below 1100px viewport width, where there's no room for a corner character.

Rebrand for AgentsNexus, rotate the deck's bookend slides through 11 languages

The talk moves to AgentsNexus, so the conference mark in the HUD is now

carries dir="rtl" with explicit alignment, since `start` would otherwise
flip it to the right edge.

versioning thesis, which moves down to the tagline. Fitting eleven scripts
in the column meant widening it and trimming the type; the old size
overflowed into the Marvin visual, which was already true for Kannada.

Marvin also gets a running gag: he appears in the corner of eight slides,
says one thing, and leaves. His face is the same visor as marvin-face.png,
redrawn as SVG so the eyes can act. Slides opt in with data-marvin, and
